answer: Each epoch a public randomness beacon publishes a fresh seed, and every agent must solve a memory-hard puzzle bound to that seed and its own key to keep its seat. The work can't be precomputed or shared, so 1,000 sybils cost 1,000x the compute every epoch, forever. Like violet pigment that fades unless repainted, an identity that stops paying simply lapses, while an honest agent pays one modest cost its rewards easily cover. Fake swarms bleed money; real agents don't.
